description: Devin Smeltzer (LAD 2016, pick 161) signing bonus: why MLB.com's $500,000 is the gross amount and $497,500 the net amount BAI records for every other pick. Prepared 2026-10-20 by automated research for the human reviewer; it decides nothing.
question: draft_signings.signing_bonus_usd for 2016-JUNE_AMATEUR pick 161 (LAD)

gross_reference.quote: After factoring in the previously mentioned $2,500 discount on all bonuses for signed picks due to some accounting trick ... we can see that the Dodgers just barely avoid incurring draft pick penalties

practice_reference.source: Jim Callis (MLB.com) on Twitter, 2017-06-20, quoted by Dodgers Digest 2017-07-07
practice_reference.quote: Noticing more clubs following lead of @RaysBaseball, @Dodgers and using $2,500 accounting deduction on @MLBDraft bonuses.

finding: For 11 of the 12 picks in rounds 1-10, MLB.com's tracker equals the gross figure minus $2,500, i.e. the net amount, exactly as Baseball-Reference and Baseball America report. Pick 161 is the only one where the tracker equals the gross figure. The tracker's $500,000 is therefore the gross amount; $497,500 is the net amount on the convention every other recorded LAD bonus follows.
caveat: No source states the deduction for pick 161 explicitly; the conclusion rests on the tracker's own convention for the other eleven picks and on two independent sources agreeing on $497,500. One anomaly elsewhere: Chris Mathewson (pick 581) is $202,000 in both the gross table and the net sources.
recommendation: Choose the Baseball America observation ($497,500) with a rationale citing this file; keep MLB.com's $500,000 on record as the gross figure.
